We establish the connection between two distinct approaches to defining fixpoint logics: one based on monadic second-order (MSO) formulas extended with fixed points, and the other on regular tree languages extended with fixed points. We demonstrate that any fixpoint logic capable of expressing a specific class of MSO formulas with fixed points must likewise be able to express a corresponding class of regular tree formulas with fixed points, and vice versa. Furthermore, we prove an exponential-time upper bound on the satisfiability checking for these logpops, noting that this bound aligns with the best-known results for the monadic second-order framework.

Recovering signals or images from limited measurements is a critical challenge in many fields, with sparse representations being a particularly effective approach. This paper introduces a new Bayesian framework for sparse reconstruction that utilizes a conjugate prior, specifically a multivariate Student's t-distribution, to model sparsity-inducing hyperpriors. The resulting sparsity model is defined by its ability to be factorized into two components: a standard Gaussian prior and a precision matrix inverse. This structural factorization facilitates the derivation of an efficient Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm for parameter estimation. The precision of the proposed method is validated through numerical experiments on synthetic data and real-world MRI scans.

The expanding use of mobile devices and the rising popularity of citizen science have created a new avenue for monitoring air quality. This study introduces a "drive-by sensing" approach that utilizes mobile platforms to gather atmospheric data. The proposed method employs a sensor fusion technique to identify and track pollution hotspots, which are subsequently visualized on a digital map. The system's efficacy is demonstrated through the analysis of data collected from a fleet of vehicles.

This paper presents the Weil representation of the Weil type for the generalized special linear group acting on finite fields, specifically over $\mathbb{F}_q$. It establishes a connection between the Weil representation of the generalized special linear group and that of the generalized semi-direct product group formed by combining general linear groups with Witt vectors. Furthermore, it defines the Weil representation of the generalized compact group structure involving general linear groups and semi-direct products, and proves the equivalence between the Weil representation of the generalized special linear group and those of general linear groups and Witt vectors.

Persuasive videos are widely used in marketing, education, and entertainment, yet their creation typically demands expert knowledge and significant time and effort. To address this, we introduce Persuade, a novel AI-driven framework for automatically producing persuasive videos. Our approach relies on three core components: (1) a multi-modal sentiment analysis module that identifies sentiment-bearing words and images; (2) a persuasive video retrieval module that locates relevant video clips based on the analyzed sentiment and textual context; and (3) a persuasive video editing module that assembles these media elements into a coherent, persuasive final video. Experiments conducted on a newly curated dataset demonstrate that Persuade effectively generates high-quality persuasive videos.

We introduce a TDVP (time-dependent variational principle) approach for modeling the dynamics of trapped ions. This method is designed to simulate both the evolution of a single ion and systems comprising multiple ions. By employing a tensor network representation of the state, the approach derives equations of motion for the variational parameters. The resulting equations of motion are second-order in time, enabling the precise tracking of dynamics even when subjected to strong driving forces. The approach is validated through comparisons with exact numerical solutions for small ion arrays and through the analysis of strong-driving regimes for individual ions.

The computational neuroscience field has recently seen a surge in the use of parameter exploration techniques, driven by the need to identify biologically plausible values for models. High Performance Computing (HPC) is essential for this work, yet many researchers in the domain lack access to it. This paper outlines the implementation of a parameter exploration method on the NERSC's Perseus cluster, a GPU-accelerated supercomputer. The approach involves porting the code to CUDA, optimizing performance, and deploying the resulting application within an HPC environment. The study evaluates the impact of parallelization and demonstrates that GPU-based parallelization significantly enhances the speed of the parameter exploration process.

This paper introduces CAMO++, a large-scale dataset comprising 1,000 images with high-resolution instance masks for camouflaged objects. It is designed to facilitate research in camouflaged instance segmentation, a task that is significantly more difficult than standard instance segmentation because the object boundaries are often indistinct and the target color closely matches the background. To enhance the difficulty level, we also created a novel evaluation metric called the Camouflaged Instance Segmentation F1 (CIS-F1) score. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our dataset effectively assesses the performance of state-of-the-art segmentation models. Additionally, we developed a new multi-scale feature fusion network, named CAMO++-Net, which achieves state-of-the-art results on the CAMO++ collection.

This study investigates Lorentz violation within superconductors, specifically examining its influence on Ginzburg-Landau theory. We demonstrate that the model's fundamental parameters—including the magnetic susceptibility, penetration depth, and Ginzburg-Landau constant—are altered by Lorentz-violating effects. Furthermore, we derive an updated expression for the London magnetization that incorporates these corrections.

End-users frequently rely on online platforms to report issues with AI systems, yet these collections often suffer from a lack of standardization and consistency. This paper introduces a novel approach to leveraging user-generated reports to identify systematic failures within AI models. Our method focuses on extracting and categorizing user complaints into a unified framework, enabling the detection of patterns that might otherwise remain hidden. By analyzing these structured failures, we demonstrate that such reports can reveal nuanced insights into how an AI system performs in practice. Our findings indicate that aggregated end-user feedback can significantly aid in diagnosing root causes, thereby facilitating the development of more robust and reliable models.

This paper introduces a novel approach to object detection that utilizes a single decision head for the entire image, eliminating the need for multiple heads to process individual proposals. By employing a specific proposal generation strategy, the method ensures that every object within an image is fully covered by at least one proposal box. Furthermore, a specialized feature extraction mechanism is implemented to guarantee that this decision head can accurately classify objects across proposals of varying sizes and shapes. Experimental results indicate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the COCO dataset, surpassing the YOLOv4 model by 0.7% in mean average precision (mAP).

Adversarial training has become a standard approach for enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks, yet it suffers from catastrophic overfitting, where models fail to generalize to unseen adversarial examples. This paper introduces a novel method called Adversarial Dropout (ADVODROP), which improves generalization by randomly deactivating a portion of the model's neurons during training. We demonstrate that this technique effectively mitigates catastrophic overfitting and surpasses the performance of conventional adversarial training. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of ADVODROP, establishing its robustness against various attack strategies.

Thakurta black holes are theoretical solutions to Einstein's equations that represent charged black holes surrounded by a thin spherical shell of charged matter. This study explores the physical conditions necessary for the formation of Thakurta black holes within our universe. We examine the characteristics of the charged fluid comprising the shell and demonstrate that, under specific conditions, this fluid can be realized as a phantom fluid. Furthermore, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of these black holes, specifically their heat capacity, and analyze the implications for black hole physics.

This paper investigates continuous-time optimization frameworks where objectives switch indefinitely over time. Such scenarios are prevalent in distributed machine learning, where goals fluctuate between minimizing local loss and managing communication costs, or between minimizing global loss and satisfying consensus constraints. While prior research has extensively analyzed these problems under fixed objectives, the continuous-time switching of objectives introduces significant complexity. We introduce a novel algorithm capable of handling persistent objective switches, achieving an approximation error bounded by a constant multiple of the switching frequency. This result is supported by a rigorous convergence analysis, which demonstrates that the generated trajectory converges to a specific subset of the objective's level sets. This analysis relies on a new concept called the "weak Lyapunov property," which is defined and applied to a specific class of smooth, nonconvex, and nonscaled functions.

Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables computations on encrypted data without decryption, with bootstrapping serving as a key technique to overcome inherent depth limits. While current HE schemes face significant latency and memory overhead during bootstrapping, the NTRU prime scheme has recently demonstrated the ability to execute bootstrapping with minimal ciphertext expansion. This study introduces a new method to achieve NTRU-based bootstrapping that reduces the expansion of ciphertexts even further. We utilize the NTRU hardware accelerator (NHE) to implement this approach, evaluating its performance across various parameter sets. The results indicate that our method outperforms the NTRU-based approach by a factor of 2.5x, with the 8192 parameter set achieving a 3.5x improvement.

This work examines a real symmetric, rotationally invariant random matrix ensemble featuring a confining logarithmic potential, $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{\alpha=1}^d x_i^\alpha \ln(x_i^\alpha)$. We derive the corresponding probability distribution for the eigenvalues and calculate the partition function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in the thermodynamic limit, the eigenvalue density takes a semi-circle form.

The non-orthogonality of quantum states serves as a fundamental resource for numerous quantum protocols, including quantum key distribution, superdense coding, and quantum teleportation. While bipartite non-orthogonal correlations are typically equivalent to entanglement, in high-dimensional systems they can manifest as a distinct form of quantum correlation known as nonbipartite entanglement. This study investigates the properties of this phenomenon within a tripartite framework. We demonstrate that, unlike in bipartite scenarios, nonbipartite entanglement is not universally convertible to pure-state-based protocols. Instead, we propose a hybrid classical-quantum protocol that utilizes mixed-state nonbipartite entanglement to achieve the three-party quantum operation of the superposition of local operations and classical communication (SLOCC). This work represents the first demonstration of such a superposition protocol operating on mixed-state quantum correlations.

We demonstrate that factorization of local causal influences is not a fundamental requirement for deriving Bell's inequalities; rather, this condition is superfluous because a more rigorous interpretation of local causality inherently entails factorization. Consequently, any theory upholding local causality must satisfy the requirement of factorization. Additionally, we present a revised derivation of Bell's theorem that relies entirely on standard elements of causal modeling, thereby eliminating the ambiguities found in Bell's original formulation and clarifying how local causality leads to the inequality.

This paper introduces a continuous-time video generator that produces smooth video streams by synthesizing frames along an arbitrary time trajectory. By learning a continuous, multi-scale temporal representation from short clips, the system enables the synthesis of videos with variable frame rates and durations. The proposed method outperforms existing discrete video synthesis techniques by allowing for smooth frame interpolation, the generation of videos at variable frame rates, and the ability to extrapolate videos beyond the original clip's duration.
This paper presents a novel proof of the theta correspondence for finite real reductive dual pairs, grounded in the preservation of local theta correspondence under degeneration.

Thermoluminescence dosimetry (TLD) is a widely used technique for quantifying radiation exposure from ionizing sources. This study investigates the impact of heat on the TLD material's sensitivity, specifically examining how the pre-irradiation thermal treatment affects the exposure response. The research utilizes lithium fluoride (LiF) TLDs, which are irradiated with defined radiation doses and subsequently subjected to various heating protocols. The outcomes indicate that thermal pretreatment significantly alters the sensitivity of the dosimeters, with sensitivity increasing as the temperature of the heat treatment rises.
This study examines a double phase problem characterized by a reaction term, deriving a general solution framework for such issues within the context of the double phase reaction problem.

The contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) is a fundamental metric for evaluating image quality in systems. This study introduces a method to assess the CNR of a linear shift-invariant (LSI) imaging system by utilizing the Fourier transform of the image power spectrum (IPS). The proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations and an experimental setup involving a camera equipped with a color filter array (CFA). The results demonstrate that the suggested method can effectively estimate the CNR of arbitrary LSI systems, even when the input signal is unknown. Furthermore, the method is applicable to the estimation of CNR in the context of CFAs and various imaging systems.

Machine learning models are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains, such as healthcare and finance, where their decisions must be justified. While post hoc explanations are frequently employed to provide these justifications, they often fail to accurately reflect the underlying model behavior. To address this, we introduce a framework for generating explanations that are both faithful and robust. Our approach begins by identifying a set of representative data points for each class, then uses them to train a separate classifier that mimics the original model. This surrogate model is optimized to align with the original model's outputs on the representative set while maintaining fidelity. We demonstrate that this method outperforms existing approaches in producing more accurate and stable explanations.

Although neural networks are widely used for various tasks, their decision-making processes remain opaque. To address this, numerous explanation methods have emerged, yet they typically focus on individual instances, ignoring the ability to generalize insights across multiple examples. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that generates explanations for entire datasets by creating a dataset-specific concept space. This space enables the visualization of how input data is distributed and how it is classified. We validate this method using a variety of real-world datasets, demonstrating its capacity to uncover and represent global patterns in data.

This study examines the electronic ground state of Tb$^{3+}$ ions within the tetragonal compound TbInO$_3$ using high-resolution polarized light spectroscopy. The Tb$^{3+}$ ground state is identified as a $^6H_{5/2}$ doublet, which is predominantly characterized by the $|J_z = \pm 5/2\rangle$ component. This conclusion is derived from the observation of a strong absorption peak at 26,000 cm$^{-1}$ in polarized light spectra, a feature that aligns with the theoretical excitation energy from $|J_z = \pm 5/2\rangle$ to the $^5D_4$ excited state.

This study establishes the existence of convex ancient solutions in power-of-mean curvature flows for dimensions $m \ge 2$ and powers $p > 1/2$, thereby broadening findings from previous work by B. Chow and L. Wang. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these convex solutions exhibit a singulation of type I.

This paper introduces a new convolutional neural network architecture that leverages the computational advantages of performing element-wise multiplications in the frequency domain to create a highly efficient, low-complexity design. The proposed framework utilizes a frequency-mapping approach to transform the input signal and filters into the spectral domain, where the convolutional operation is simplified into a series of multiplications. The study evaluates the performance of this method across various CNN-based tasks, including image classification and object detection, demonstrating that the architecture achieves high accuracy with significantly reduced computational costs.

Deep clustering has gained significant attention for its ability to achieve high performance in unsupervised domain adaptation. While existing approaches typically rely on a single layer within the deep network, our research demonstrates that utilizing multi-layer representations can further enhance results. We introduce a novel framework for deep clustering that integrates a multi-layer structure with a multi-objective optimization strategy. This framework employs a multi-task learning architecture to simultaneously optimize two distinct objectives: the first ensures that the deep network learns robust, transferable features, while the second guarantees that the clustering layer captures discriminative representations. By addressing both goals concurrently, our method effectively balances the trade-off between feature transferability and clustering distinctiveness. Comprehensive experiments on standard benchmarks confirm that this approach outperforms current state-of-the-art deep clustering methods in unsupervised domain adaptation.

This article details the development of a risk identification framework for the United Nations University. It outlines key characteristics such as comprehensiveness, clarity, feasibility, adaptability, and alignment with ISO 31000 standards. Furthermore, the document presents the specific risk identification tools and methodologies employed, along with a detailed overview of the process execution within the organization.

Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is a rapidly expanding field within data science that leverages concepts from algebraic topology to extract insights from data. A core component of TDA is persistent homology, which identifies topological traits across varying scales within a dataset. This study investigates the application of persistent homology for dataset classification. We introduce a methodology that integrates topological features derived from TDA with a standard Random Forest classifier. Our findings demonstrate that this hybrid approach outperforms a classifier relying solely on the topological features. Furthermore, we validate this approach using a real-world dataset from the field of astrophysics.

This paper presents process theories grounded in the framework of congruences between transition systems. These theories are defined by congrasembliness, a relation that generalizes both strong bisimilarity and coersion; unlike contrasimilarity (a relation where bisimilarity is a specific instance), contrasimilarity is not required to be an equivalence. Processes within these theories are modeled as labeled trees, and congrusimilarity is defined by a specific algorithm that compares the structural and local attributes of such trees. Furthermore, we demonstrate that process theories can be constructed by aggregating the theories derived from individual finite transition systems.

We construct a string 2-group representation that acts on the space of smooth lifts of the frame bundle for a string manifold. This action is defined by a specific 3-form valued in Lie algebra-valued differential forms on the manifold. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this representation is equivariant under the action of the string group and establishes a homomorphism into the group of bundle automorphisms.

This study examines the nonlinear behavior of ion-acoustic waves (IAWs) within a magnetized multi-ion plasma environment, specifically one containing cold positive ions, negative ions, and a distribution of thermal positive ions. The model incorporates a Maxwellian distribution for the thermal positive ions and a kappa distribution for the remaining nonthermal positive ions. Using the reductive perturbation method, the study derives the Korteweg-de Vries-Zakharov-Kuznetsov (KdV-ZK) equation to analyze the nonlinear evolution of these waves. The results indicate that fundamental IAW characteristics, such as modulational instability, ion-acoustic rogue waves, and soliton properties, are governed by plasma parameters including the fractions of negative and thermal positive ions, the nonthermal parameter kappa, and the magnetic field strength. Findings reveal that increasing the thermal positive ion fraction or the magnetic field intensity reduces the threshold for modulational instability, whereas increasing the nonthermal parameter kappa enhances this instability threshold. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the plasma conditions analyzed here support the generation of ion-acoustic solitons and the emergence of rogue waves.

Alvén waves are ubiquitous in plasmas and are extensively researched in astrophysics and fusion physics. This study examines the behavior of these waves within a cold, magnetized plasma that is inhomogeneous and exhibits spatial variations in the magnetic field. The analysis employs the WKB method, which is valid for waves with sufficiently short wavelengths. The results demonstrate that the derived WKB equations align with those obtained using the method of weighted residual (MWR). Furthermore, the WKB approach yields specific solutions, and the paper applies this method to a scenario involving a linearly varying magnetic field.

This study examines the impact of ambipolar diffusion on the evolution of a filamentary molecular cloud modeled as a self-gravitating, isothermal, one-dimensional cylinder. We derive a linear perturbation theory applicable to such systems and calculate the corresponding growth rate for the self-gravitational-ambipolar-thermal instability. Our analysis indicates that while ambipolar diffusion initially hinders instability growth, it subsequently accelerates it once the filament's mass surpasses a specific threshold. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the mass of the resulting core is governed by the ambipolar Jeans mass, which scales with the filament's density.

This study investigates the quantum coherence of a two-qubit system within the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix, focusing on the relationship between measurement direction and spin interactions. We demonstrate that whether the measurement direction aligns with or differs from the spin interactions significantly impacts these specific off-diagonal terms. Additionally, we reveal that the system's coherence is not merely a function of spin interactions but also critically depends on the spatial orientation of the measurement direction.

This paper introduces a novel, computationally efficient method for trajectory planning in multi-agent systems, designed to ensure collision-free operation. The proposed approach constructs safe corridors for each agent, where the resulting linear paths are derived by calculating the convex hulls of the trajectories. These corridors are established through a linear optimization framework that minimizes the sum of squared distances between the planned paths and the agents' reference trajectories. The convex hull constraint is managed using a cutting-plane algorithm, while the overall problem is solved via second-order cone programming. Numerical simulations demonstrate the method's effectiveness in a multi-agent environment, highlighting its efficiency and scalability.

Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) is a promising strategy for addressing the data scarcity and domain shift inherent in autonomous driving tasks, specifically lane detection. However, lane detection presents unique challenges compared to other vision tasks, primarily due to the scarcity of lane pixels and the presence of unlabeled ground truth. These characteristics complicate the use of standard techniques like pixel-level adversarial training and feature alignment. To overcome these hurdles, we introduce a novel approach that first employs a lane point cloud representation to facilitate effective domain adaptation. Additionally, we develop a specialized loss function designed to align the latent space of lane features. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the Cityscapes and XDrive datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions.

This study examines the absorption dynamics of water droplets on a hydrogel surface, specifically focusing on how the initial concentration of adsorbed particles influences the time required for complete wetting. Theoretical analysis reveals that the droplet's absorption time scales with the square root of the initial particle concentration. These predictions are validated through experiments using a mixture of hydrogel and fluorescent particles, where absorption time is measured via fluorescence microscopy. The results confirm the theoretical model, showing that the absorption time is indeed proportional to the square root of the initial particle concentration.

The relationship between academic performance and collaboration is complex, as it is influenced by various contextual factors such as the learning environment, course type, and cultural background. This study examines how these factors affect performance outcomes by analyzing data from 1,600 students across 25 distinct courses. We employ a hierarchical Bayesian model to estimate individual performance and collaboration levels, while simultaneously accounting for course-level characteristics. Our results indicate that collaboration is a strong predictor of performance, yet this link is moderated by specific contextual variables. Additionally, we demonstrate that integrating contextual features into the model significantly reduces the variance of performance estimates. Ultimately, these insights highlight the necessity of accounting for context when investigating the link between performance and collaboration, and offer a scalable framework for analyzing academic data from diverse sources.

Radar Wind Profilers (RWP) are highly effective for atmospheric research due to their ability to operate effectively in all-weather conditions and their capability to function without the need for cooling systems. This study introduces a novel method for estimating the vertical distribution of atmospheric temperature by utilizing the power spectrum of the radar return. We developed a theoretical model that correlates the power spectrum of the radar return with the vertical temperature profile, which is then solved using an iterative technique. We evaluated the proposed method using data from a 24 GHz VHF radar, and our results indicate that the temperature profile can be determined with a resolution of approximately 100 meters.

We present a comprehensive study of the stellar distribution within the globular cluster NGC 6388, utilizing a 1.5-hour deep exposure from the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys. This dataset, combined with a 1.5-hour exposure from the Wide Field Camera 3, allows for the identification of faint stars down to a V magnitude of approximately 25.5. By analyzing the spatial distribution of these stars, we have determined the cluster's core radius and its extended tidal radius. Our findings indicate that the cluster's core radius is 0.20 arcseconds, while its tidal radius is 1.0 arcsecond. Additionally, we have identified a tidal stream of stars surrounding the cluster, which suggests that NGC 6388 is a member of a larger stellar stream. Finally, we have estimated the cluster's age to be approximately 12 billion years.

This study explores the utility of synthetic translations for bilingual text mining. Specifically, we evaluate whether synthetic pairs can enhance the quality of reference translations and whether bilingual mining can effectively leverage existing parallel datasets. Our results indicate that utilizing a synthetic bilingual corpus significantly improves reference translation accuracy and that integrating structured mining techniques with unstructured approaches yields superior performance compared to relying solely on unstructured methods.

We investigate the entanglement scaling of a one-dimensional quantum Ising model subject to dissipation, specifically examining the influence of varying interaction strengths on the decay of Ising order. Our analysis demonstrates that the interplay between coherent unitary dynamics and dissipative dynamics can alter the entanglement scaling exponents. Specifically, in regimes dominated by dissipation, the entanglement between spins decays exponentially with distance, whereas in unitary-dominated regimes, it follows a power-law decay.

We have developed a theoretical framework to analyze the band structures of van der Waals heterobilayers, specifically accounting for the interplay between interlayer hybridization and the band-edge exciton. This approach is applied to MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayers, revealing that applying a perpendicular electric field can suppress this hybridization, leading to a significant reduction in the band-edge exciton's excitonic coupling. This finding offers a viable method for investigating the physics of excitons in such hybrid structures under the influence of the field.

This study examines the echo state property (ESP) within the framework of quantum reservoir computing (QRC). We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the ESP to hold in QRC systems, specifically addressing both finite-dimensional and quantum Gaussian models. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the parallelized QRC architecture effectively emulates the echo state property through the convergence of the quantum channel's Kossakowski-Nakagawa-Suzuki (KNS) semigroup. Leveraging these theoretical findings, we construct a QRC architecture designed for the classification of handwritten digits. The results confirm that this parallelized QRC achieves high accuracy in digit classification.

Hybrid photon-atom integrated platforms featuring trapped, individually addressable neutral atoms offer significant promise for quantum information processing. This work introduces a new architecture that merges the advantages of photonic circuits with those of trapped neutral atoms. We demonstrate that hybrid circuits can be constructed by combining standard photonic components with hybrid systems that couple photons to individual neutral atoms via light-matter interactions. These hybrid systems can be fabricated using established nanofabrication techniques, making them compatible with existing photonic infrastructure. Furthermore, we outline a method to achieve deterministic coupling between remote, trapped neutral atoms by utilizing a hybrid circuit to exchange a single photon. This approach enables the creation of complex, hybrid quantum systems that combine the high-fidelity, long-lived quantum memory of trapped neutral atoms with the rapid, high-fidelity photonic operations facilitated by photonic circuits.

This study presents a comparative analysis of various finite element formulations for the Laplace problem, utilizing the $h$-refinement strategy to evaluate their performance. The analysis focuses on the $L^2$ error, the condition number, and the speed of convergence in solving the Poisson equation. The specific methods examined include the standard Galerkin approach, the interior penalty method, and the discontinuous Galerkin method.

This study examines a cosmological framework where the interaction between dark energy and dark matter is modeled using a logarithmic coupling function. We analyze the resulting fixed points of the background evolution and stability of dark energy halos. Our findings indicate that while a quintessence model with a logarithmic coupling function can exhibit unstable critical points, the corresponding stable critical points for a phantom quintessence model are unstable. Furthermore, we find that a stable phantom quintessence dark energy model with a stable critical point is impossible. We also explore the evolution of dark matter and the impact of dark energy on the matter density parameter. Finally, we discuss the implications of our results for the late-time accelerated expansion of the universe.

Optical tidal disruption events (TDEs) are characterized by the sudden brightening of galaxies due to tidal disruption, accompanied by outflows that are often detected via broad emission lines. We present a new TDE, designated AT2020jys, which exhibits a significant blue shift in the H$\alpha$ line, indicating a high-velocity outflow. This event was initially identified in the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) survey on 2020 June 13.05, with a peak magnitude of $g$ = 15.1. AT2020jys is located in the dwarf galaxy NGC 4649, a known host of the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (AGN) 3C 273.1. The event's light curve displays a rapid rise and a slow decline, with a rise time of approximately 10 days and a half-life of roughly 100 days. The broad emission lines, which are initially blue-shifted, gradually revert to a neutral state over a period of about 100 days. We propose that this blue shift results from a high-velocity outflow driven by the interaction between the tidal disruption ejecta and the circumstellar medium. The event's light curve and spectral evolution are consistent with a tidal disruption scenario involving a massive star, specifically one with a mass of approximately 100 solar masses.

This study introduces a new acoustic pressure formulation designed to accurately model the propagation of waves from oscillating micro-bubbles. These bubbles generate significant local pressure fluctuations that standard far-field approximations fail to capture. The proposed method integrates the acoustic wave equation with a Helmholtz-type boundary integral equation, employing a dipole-type double-layer kernel. This kernel is derived by applying multipole expansion to the conventional integral formulation, which previously struggled with slow convergence due to bubble proximity to the discretization boundary. By utilizing a dipole expansion, the new approach ensures rapid convergence. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through numerical simulations of an acoustically driven micro-bubble, with results benchmarked against direct solutions of the acoustic wave equation.

Stress plays a pivotal role in regulating and expressing human emotions, a connection that is critical for advancing human-computer interaction. While recent research has established links between stress and physiological signals such as heart rate, blood pressure, and electrodermal activity, this study specifically investigates the relationship between stress and the electroencephalogram (EEG). We introduce a novel deep learning framework designed to classify stress levels from EEG data, utilizing a hybrid of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The proposed model achieved a classification accuracy of 94.14%, outperforming existing methods. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of varying hyperparameters on model performance, alongside an analysis of the most influential EEG channels and frequency bands. The findings demonstrate that the temporal information captured by the LSTM component is essential for achieving high accuracy.

Pan-GEA is a toolkit designed for annotating spatial navigation tasks, including the navigation of both humans and AI agents, within textual and graphical environments. This paper introduces the tool, demonstrates its utility by annotating a dataset of navigation tasks for AI training, and establishes a preliminary benchmark for AI research in this domain.

Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are pivotal for cosmology, yet their progenitor systems remain uncertain. This study investigates the link between SNe Ia and star formation timescales (SFT) in massive elliptical galaxies, utilizing a sample of 1,000 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) with stellar masses exceeding $10^{11} M_{\odot}$. We employ a semi-analytic model to determine the SFT of these galaxies, utilizing the observed SNe Ia rates from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Palomar Transient Factory (PTF). Our findings indicate that the SFT of massive elliptical galaxies is governed by the star formation history of the early universe, specifically the period between redshifts $z=2$ and $z=0$. Consequently, the SFT in these galaxies is primarily determined by the star formation rate (SFR) of the universe during this epoch, leading to a strong correlation between SFT and the cumulative SFR integrated from $z=2$ to $z=0$. This correlation implies that the SNe Ia rate in these galaxies is strongly influenced by the star formation history of the universe. We further examine the relationship between SFT and the SFR density of the universe, finding that the SFT is closely tied to the star formation rate density of the universe. Compressive sensing (CS) has emerged as a highly effective approach for image reconstruction, particularly valued for its low computational cost and high efficiency. However, achieving high-quality reconstructions with sparse representation remains challenging. While nonconvex regularization offers a solution by balancing sparsity and reconstruction accuracy, it is computationally demanding and often difficult to optimize. To address this, we introduce a new nonconvex regularizer called the $\log$-sum function, which is both efficient to compute and easy to optimize. We further develop an iterative algorithm based on the majorization-minimization framework to solve the CS reconstruction problem using this regularizer. Theoretical analysis confirms that the resulting reconstruction converges to a stationary point. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves reconstruction performance comparable to state-of-the-art techniques while significantly reducing computational complexity.

Detecting skin lesions on faces is a vital component of diagnosing dermatological conditions. While existing facial skin lesion detection methods typically rely on binary classification, they often fail to capture the intricate contextual information necessary for accurate semantic segmentation. To address this, we introduce a novel framework for facial skin lesion semantic segmentation that integrates a binary classifier with a segmentation network. This approach utilizes a multi-scale feature extraction module to enhance the model's ability to identify lesions across various scales. Additionally, we developed a specialized loss function that combines binary cross-entropy with Dice loss, designed to mitigate the challenge of class imbalance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in facial skin lesion detection.

This paper introduces a new class of block codes, termed PAC codes, which are designed to be more efficient than both 5G polar codes and traditional convolutional codes. The study provides a detailed description of the code's structure, its encoding and decoding algorithms, and presents simulation results that highlight its superior performance.

Sequential recommenders are designed to forecast future user interactions by leveraging historical behavior sequences. However, a significant hurdle for these models is the data sparsity encountered with cold-start users, who possess no prior interaction history. Although recent research has addressed this issue by integrating external data sources, it often fails to capture the nuanced semantic relationships between sequential actions. To overcome this, we introduce a novel framework that merges sequential recommendation with knowledge graph embedding. This approach utilizes a knowledge graph comprising user-item relations and item attributes, enhanced by a new embedding technique that captures both local and global item characteristics. Furthermore, we employ a multi-head attention mechanism to synthesize embeddings from various perspectives, thereby enriching the representation of sequential user actions. Extensive experiments conducted on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions.
This paper examines the potential of the Pierre Auger Observatory to investigate dark matter and cosmological phenomena through the analysis of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays.

Capturing facial identities of vehicle occupants via windshields presents a demanding challenge for face recognition systems, primarily due to the combined effects of glass reflection, glass refraction, and the variable viewing angles typical in real-world settings. This paper introduces a novel method for recognizing vehicle occupants captured through windshields, a technique previously absent from existing literature. Our approach begins by employing a specialized network to isolate and correct reflections, thereby eliminating ghosting artifacts. Subsequently, we present a new facial representation framework that integrates both facial structure and texture details. This representation is evaluated using a dedicated loss function, which is trained on a newly constructed dataset comprising 1,000 vehicles with 1,000 distinct individuals. Extensive testing demonstrates that our approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art solutions.

This paper details the design and implementation of a custom, open-source code repository system for the Python language, named 'python-bazaar,' which functions as a dedicated package repository. It serves as a comprehensive case study for software engineering researchers and practitioners interested in custom code management solutions. The document also presents a set of design principles regarding the creation of open-source code repositories, which can guide the development of similar projects in various programming languages.

This study addresses the challenge of multiple missing predictors in data, a scenario where a substantial number of covariates are absent. We introduce a novel approach that integrates the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm with a Bayesian method for model selection. This framework enables the identification of a parsimonious model that effectively captures the underlying data-generating process while simultaneously recovering missing variables. We rigorously demonstrate that the resulting estimator is consistent and that the algorithm converges to a global maximum. Furthermore, we develop a hybrid algorithm that leverages the strengths of both the EM method and gradient descent to enhance computational efficiency. Empirical evaluations using both simulated datasets and a real-world application confirm that the proposed technique outperforms existing methods in terms of performance.

We introduce Decomposed Inductive Procedure Learning (DIPL), a new learning framework that mimics human learning rates by utilizing the inference of simpler procedures to approximate complex ones. Our analysis of the DIPL algorithm on the MNIST dataset demonstrates that it achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods.

The rise of fabricated or misleading content, particularly that generated by machines, has become a growing threat to society. To address this issue, researchers have developed various techniques to identify deceptive text. However, current methods are limited by their reliance on specific datasets, which restricts their ability to generalize effectively to novel data. This paper introduces a novel approach to tackle the challenge of identifying fake news and machine-generated content using a multi-task learning framework. By leveraging shared information across multiple related tasks, our method achieves improved performance. We conduct extensive experiments on two distinct datasets to validate our approach. The findings demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, confirming its efficacy in detecting both fake news and artificially generated text.

This paper investigates torsion structures for elliptic curves defined over the compositum of all $D_4$ extensions over $\mathbb{Q}$. Our findings indicate that this specific field excludes certain torsion structures. Furthermore, we provide examples of elliptic curves over $D_4$ fields that exhibit a rank of 3.

This study examines the dynamics of a non-uniform qubit array where a single element is continuously driven on resonance. The authors demonstrate that, contrary to expectations, this setup can generate a collective response in undriven qubits, a phenomenon that is tunable via non-local interactions. The analysis reveals that this effect is governed by the interplay between the driving field's detuning and the non-local interaction strengths. The researchers also explore the relationship between this effect and the system's eigenstates, providing a comprehensive understanding of how coherent interactions propagate across spatially heterogeneous qubit ensembles.

A crawler is designed to discover web pages by following links, with a focused crawler specifically aiming to locate pages relevant to a specific topic. This paper introduces a focused crawler that utilizes a pre-trained language model to identify pages pertinent to a user's query. The proposed approach, named Language-Model-driven Focused Crawling (LMFC), operates by generating a set of seed pages based on the query and then retrieving new relevant pages through graph-based community detection. This method offers two primary advantages: first, it requires no additional pre-training for the language model, relying instead on the inherent capabilities of an off-the-shelf model; second, it employs community detection to efficiently locate pertinent pages even when they are situated deep within the graph structure. Experiments conducted on the Twitter API demonstrate that LMFC surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of recall, while maintaining comparable levels of precision.

Process mining techniques are increasingly employed to analyze event data within information systems, a method that has proven effective for uncovering process models, identifying procedural bottlenecks, and detecting deviations. However, process mining is not without its limitations; notably, the volume of data required to accurately reconstruct process models can be prohibitive. This requirement is particularly problematic in scenarios where events are logged at a granular level, such as the transactional level, resulting in an overwhelming number of records. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel data aggregation technique that leverages information theory to reduce the total event volume. This approach is applied to a real-world case study of a large-scale online retailer, demonstrating that the proposed method can significantly decrease the dataset size while maintaining the process model's fidelity.

Low-rank factorization has proven effective for seismic data processing, yet it struggles with high-frequency signals, which are inherently more full-rank. To address this, we introduce a new low-rank constraint designed to enhance the processing of such higher-frequency seismic data. By deriving the necessary optimality conditions for seismic wavefields, we develop an iterative algorithm to solve the constrained optimization problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this approach effectively improves both the quality of common-depth sections and horizontal common-offset traces.

Metalenses are widely utilized for focusing light, yet they typically suffer from significant chromatic and off-axis aberrations. This study introduces a novel metalens design featuring a quadratic phase profile, which inherently eliminates these defects. We demonstrate that this architecture can be realized through a straightforward superposition of concentric zones, each composed of resonant subwavelength scatterers. By calculating the necessary scattering phase shifts for each zone, we established a design methodology for metalenses that is both simple and scalable. Furthermore, we validated this approach using a 100-$\mu$m-diameter metalence focused on a 980-nm laser beam, successfully producing a diffraction-limited spot size of 1.1 $\mu$m.

The analysis incorporates a self-consistent Poisson equation and accounts for electron and ion thermal effects. The discharge process is simulated using a particle-in-cell (PIC) code, while the temporal evolution of the resulting plasma is analyzed through a two-fluid model. The study identifies the emergence of drift-soliton-like structures within the electron fluid, which are linked to the generation of a quasi-electrostatic potential well. The research demonstrates that these potential wells are created by ions, which are confined by the diode's walls. The findings indicate that these drift-soliton-like structures are a direct result of the interaction between the diode's electric field and the plasma's thermal effects. This work examines the dynamics of tensorial gravitational perturbations and scalar fields in the vicinity of spherically symmetric black holes within the context of string theory, specifically focusing on the Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati (DGP) braneworld model and the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified gravity. We derive the corresponding quasinormal frequencies and demonstrate that the resulting corrections to the spectrum are consistent with the high-energy string theory limits. Furthermore, we establish the appropriate boundary conditions for both tensorial and scalar fields and employ the asymptotic iteration method to compute the quasinormal modes.

The pulsar backscatter of gravitational waves (GWs) is a promising avenue for detecting the stochastic GW background (GWs) and measuring the speed of gravity. However, the pulsar timing array (PTA) community has not yet reached a consensus on the statistical methods required to make a definitive claim regarding the detection of this background. This paper addresses that gap by applying Bayesian inference to the pulsar data from the Parkes PTA. We demonstrate that the current data are insufficient to make a robust detection claim or to place meaningful upper limits on the GW background. Furthermore, we find that the current data cannot constrain the speed of gravity to be compatible with general relativity.

This study examines generator matrices of minimum distance $d$ whose supports are restricted to a specific set $S$. It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of such codes for any given $S$ and $d$, alongside the development of an algorithm to determine a code's existence or compute its maximum possible dimension. Additionally, the paper derives analogous results for the support of the code's coset leaders.

This study investigates matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators within the $L^p$ space for $1 < p < \infty$. We demonstrate that a matrix-valued truncated operator is equal to $T_{\varphi}^{\mathcal H}$, where $\varphi$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb T, \mathbb C^n)$, if and only if there exists a symbol $\psi$ in the vanishing Besov space $B_{0}(\mathbb B_{n})$ such that $T_{\varphi}^{\mathcal H}$ equals $T_{\psi}^{\mathcal H}$. Furthermore, we establish that a truncated operator is identical to $T_{\varphi}^{\mathcal H}$, with $\varphi$ in the Lorentz space $L(p/2,2)$, if and only if there exists a symbol $\psi$ in the Besov space $BMO_{\infty}$ such that $T_{\varphi}^{\mathcal H}$ equals $T_{\psi}^{\mathcal H}$.

This study introduces a novel framework for multi-phase clinical trials, designed to dynamically select the most informative and decisive experiments at each stage. By integrating the multi-armed bandit approach with the concept of decision-making, our method incorporates both patient welfare and research efficiency. We evaluate the proposed framework against a baseline strategy that relies on fixed, pre-determined experiments. Our findings indicate that the dynamic selection process significantly enhances decision-making capabilities, thereby accelerating drug development timelines.

Unsupervised Anomaly Detection (UAD) aims to identify anomalies within data without relying on prior labeled examples. While recent advancements in generative models have significantly improved UAD performance, they often fail to account for the inherent class structure of data, which can lead to false positives. To address this, we introduce a new approach called Class-Structure-Aware Anomaly Detection (CSAAD). This framework leverages the intrinsic class structure of normal data to enhance detection accuracy. Specifically, we develop a novel latent space representation that incorporates class structures, enabling the model to distinguish between normal and anomalous samples more effectively. Extensive experiments across three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques.

We examine the impact of partial spin polarization on the universal thermodynamics of a SU(N) repulsive Fermi gas. By employing a renormalization group approach, we derive the phase diagram for polarized systems, revealing that the nature of the phase transition shifts from second-order to first-order as the degree of spin polarization increases.

We introduce a novel gamma-ray pulsar stacking methodology designed to identify low-luminosity pulsars with low spin-down power that remain invisible to traditional gamma-ray telescopes. This approach utilizes the temporal and spectral characteristics of the entire gamma-ray pulsar population. By analyzing the average pulse profiles of the known population, we detect a significant excess of counts in the Crab band (30–300 MeV) that exceeds the expected background by 10.8 sigma. This excess is consistent with the emission of a single, unresolved source, which we term the "Crab-band excess." The inferred properties of this hypothetical source are as follows: a spin period of 110–120 ms, a luminosity of $10^{34}$–$10^{35}$ erg s$^{-1}$, a spin-down power of $10^{35}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and a distance of 100–1,000 pc. This source is likely a young pulsar located within the Galactic plane, with a potential origin in the Cygnus region. While the source is not yet confirmed, this study represents the first stacking analysis of the gamma-ray pulsar population.

We have analyzed the magnetotransport characteristics of the 2D electron gas in GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, specifically focusing on the fractional filling factors $\nu=2/7$ and $2/9$. The study reveals that the magnetorotons associated with the $2/7$ and $2/9$ states exhibit distinct characteristics compared to those found at $\nu=1/3$ or near-half-filling. Specifically, the $2/7$ and $2/9$ peaks are notably broader and possess a lower minimum energy. These findings suggest that the quasiparticles in the $2/7$ and $2/9$ states possess reduced effective masses and lower self-energy. Additionally, the observation of a second, broader peak at a higher energy within the $2/7$ spectrum indicates the presence of a second type of broad, low-mass state.

This study investigates the Cauchy problem for the cutoff Boltzmann equation featuring the hard potential $s \in (0,1)$ and the hard-sphere cross-section $g_0 = 1$. We establish that if the initial data $f_0(x,v)$ is non-negative and belongs to the weighted space $L^1_{\{2\}}(\mathbb{R}^3_x,L^2_{\{2\}}(\mathbb{R}^3_v;w_2^2))$, then a non-negative unique mild solution $f(t,x,v)$ exists for all $t \ge 0$. This solution remains a unique element of the space $L^1_{\{2\}}(\mathbb{R}^3_x,L^2_{\{2\}}(\mathbb{R}^3_v;w_2^2))$ for all $t \ge 0$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the solution exhibits exponential decay in $L^2$ norm as $t \to \infty$.

Class-dependent labeling noise is a prevalent challenge in classification tasks, prompting the development of numerous solutions. Current mainstream strategies generally fall into two categories: those that filter out noisy labels and those that accommodate noise during the learning process. However, these methods often fail to fully leverage the specific characteristics of class-dependent labeling errors. To address this, we introduce a novel approach called "Class-Dependent Noise-Dependent" (CNDD) that integrates the strengths of both existing strategies. The methodology consists of two primary phases: first, a noise detection phase that leverages the inherent class-specific properties of the data to identify labels affected by noise; second, a noise-tolerant training phase that utilizes the detected labels to refine the learning model. Experimental results across various real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach effectively overcomes the limitations of current methods and achieves superior performance.

This study examines cyclic orbit codes defined within the field extension $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We demonstrate that the Singer subgroup of $\mathrm{PGL}(2, q^n)$ acts as the automorphism group for these codes. Furthermore, we derive the length distribution of codes comprising non-zero vectors and codes containing the zero vector separately. Additionally, we establish specific bounds regarding the Singleton distance of such codes.

We present a comprehensive study of the binary system WOCS 11028 within the M67 open cluster, utilizing high-resolution spectroscopy from the Magellan/MIKE instrument. This analysis yields precise stellar parameters, including masses of 1.11 and 1.16 solar units, and effective temperatures of 5,900 and 5,800 Kelvin for the two components. By comparing these findings with prior literature, we confirm that the system's evolutionary status remains unchanged. Furthermore, our spectral analysis reveals that the star's spectrum is free of significant blends, enabling us to determine the chemical abundances of both components. We find that WOCS 11028 exhibits a chemical composition consistent with the M67 cluster average, with no detectable anomalies.

This paper investigates the eigenfunction completeness of the complex Schr\"odinger operator defined as $L = \Delta + \alpha|x|^{-2}Q(x)$, where $\alpha$ is a real parameter and $Q(x) = \sum_{j=1}^4 c_jx_j^2$ with $c_j \in \mathbb{C}$. We demonstrate that for the condition $Re(\alpha) < 1/4$, the set of eigenfunctions is complete.

Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) is a mesh-free technique for solving partial differential equations that has gained significant traction in computational fluid dynamics. This paper introduces novel kernel-based gradient estimators that adopt an integral formulation, offering a distinct perspective on gradient estimation within SPH. We introduce two specific estimators: one that is first-order accurate and another that achieves second-order accuracy. The latter attains its higher order of precision by incorporating a constraint that the gradient must be orthogonal to the kernel's kernel surface. To address scenarios where this orthogonality constraint cannot be met exactly, we develop a robust method for solving the resulting nonlinear system. Furthermore, we propose a new kernel function that facilitates the exact satisfaction of the orthogonality condition. We demonstrate the efficacy of these estimators through numerical experiments on the 1D Burgers' equation, the Darcy flow problem, and the viscous Burgers' equation.

Spectral super-resolution (SSR) involves reconstructing the full spectral information of an image from a single RGB capture. This work introduces a new SSR framework that leverages the inherent low-rank characteristics of spectral images. Specifically, we propose a low-rank SSR method based on the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the RGB-to-spectral transformation matrix. This approach first derives the complete spectral cube by solving a constrained optimization problem. Furthermore, to enhance the robustness of the SVD process, we develop a new iterative algorithm that integrates the SSR task with low-rank approximation. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art SSR techniques in terms of accuracy.

This study introduces a novel method for geolocating street view imagery by leveraging rich metadata. We employ a two-stage approach: first, we apply image inpainting to reconstruct missing elements in satellite imagery, thereby enhancing the accuracy of visual feature matching. Second, we utilize a convolutional neural network to forecast the camera's heading angle, a critical piece of metadata. This two-pronged enhancement of visual and heading data significantly boosts the precision of our location estimation framework. Evaluations on a novel asset dataset comprising over 100,000 images demonstrate that our technique outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a median positional error of 10 meters.

This study introduces a new method for identifying dam reservoirs in remote sensing imagery, which involves two sequential tasks: first, delineating the water body boundaries, and second, extracting the dam reservoir by merging these masks with a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). The proposed approach utilizes a U-Net architecture to segment water bodies, followed by a post-processing step that integrates the resulting binary mask with the DEM to generate the final reservoir mask. This two-stage process effectively captures the intricate details of dam reservoirs, which are often difficult to delineate in a single step. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in delineating small reservoirs.

Predicting the category of points of interest (POI) based on user check-in data is a critical challenge in location-based services. While existing research has predominantly focused on textual data, it has largely overlooked the potential of visual information. This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates visual data to enhance textual representations for POI type prediction. The proposed approach employs a multi-view feature learning method to generate a unified embedding that captures both semantic and visual characteristics. Furthermore, we develop a multi-task learning strategy to jointly optimize POI type prediction and image captioning, thereby refining the learned embeddings. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a 10.3% increase in the harmonic mean of micro- and macro-averaged F1-scores.

Earnings reports serve as a vital vehicle for firms to articulate their perspectives on performance and future outlooks, thereby significantly shaping investor expectations. This study examines the impact of such reports on stock price volatility and trading volume, utilizing a proprietary dataset comprising 1.5 million+ transcripts from S&P 500 companies between 2004 and 2018. We employ a novel methodology to quantify the textual influence of these reports, which correlates specific management narratives with subsequent stock price and trading volume movements. Our findings reveal that management's choice of language regarding future prospects is a key determinant of stock price volatility and trading volume. Specifically, mentions of "good" news in these reports are associated with reduced price volatility and lower trading volume, whereas references to "bad" future outlooks correlate with increased volatility and higher trading volume.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are extensively utilized for environmental monitoring, traffic management, and surveillance. A critical aspect of these systems is sensor deployment, which involves strategically positioning sensors to ensure coverage of the target area. This study presents a new approach to WSN coverage by modeling the problem as a maximum coverage scenario for mobile elements. It introduces a new algorithm named **MCO-Coverage**, which leverages the Multi-Choice Ordered Search Heuristic to maximize the number of area units observed by these sensors. The methodology is divided into two stages: first, a clustering phase that groups sensors based on their spatial proximity; second, a coverage phase that determines the optimal placement for each cluster. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using both randomly generated test cases and real-world data. The results demonstrate that MCO-Coverage outperforms existing state-of-the-art heuristics in terms of solution quality.

Quantum Linear System Problem (QLSP) is a fundamental task in quantum computing, and the quantum adiabatic algorithm (QAA) has been proposed as a viable solution. However, the standard QAA is inherently non-unitary, which restricts its ability to achieve high precision. This study demonstrates that targeting a specific eigenstate via the QAA allows for an efficient resolution of the QLSP. We introduce a novel, state-specific quantum adiabatic algorithm that utilizes the non-adiabatic effects of the standard approach to reach a desired eigenstate. This method is tested on the inversion of a matrix representing a linear system of equations. By employing the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to drive the adiabatic evolution, the proposed scheme is evaluated using both simulated quantum and classical frameworks. Results indicate that the quantum state generated by the state-targeted algorithm closely approximates the exact eigenstate, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the new approach.

This study examines the formation of compactons and their associated subcompactons—topological nonlinear dielectric media structures—through the process of adiabatic compression. These phenomena emerge in systems governed by a nonlinear wave equation featuring a hard cubic potential. By employing a self-similar adiabatic ansatz, we derive the evolution law governing the nonlinear wave's speed as it compresses. The analysis reveals that compactons and subcompactons continuously contract under adiabatic conditions, with their velocities scaling according to a power law. Furthermore, we demonstrate that compactons can be adiabatically transformed into subcompactons, enabling the creation of topological solitons with arbitrarily small spatial widths.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of the experimental evidence supporting Beyond Standard Model (BSM) physics, focusing on anomalies observed in lepton universality ratios, the muon's anomalous magnetic moment, the neutron's electric dipole moment, and various searches for dark matter and neutrinos beyond the Standard Model. Additionally, it outlines the strategies of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and future neutrino facilities in investigating these phenomena.

We introduce a new magnetometer utilizing the $^{14}$N nuclear spins in diamond, which employs a nitrogen-vacancy (NVT) ensemble as a reference frame. This system achieves a rotation sensitivity of $0.0015^\circ/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ at a rotation rate of $100\,\text{rpm}$, a performance metric that remains constant regardless of rotation speed. This stability is achieved through a feedback loop that actively compensates for any applied rotations.

Whole-cell computational models, which simulate cellular phenotypes by integrating diverse molecular details, are essential for advancing synthetic biology. However, the sheer scale of these models, driven by extensive networks of biochemical reactions, creates significant hurdles for both construction and execution. To address this, we introduce a new modeling framework that represents cells as collections of interacting modules, each encapsulating a specific biological function. This modular architecture enables the systematic development of models and facilitates their dynamic analysis. Furthermore, we have developed a novel simulation engine capable of handling these models efficiently. To demonstrate the approach, we constructed a whole-cell model of *E. coli* and validated its simulation performance against benchmarks from the original monolithic structure.

Mobile visual search (MVS) has become increasingly popular, yet it remains challenging due to the significant domain gap between web-scale image collections and real-world user queries. While MVS typically relies on a single user image for retrieval, this approach is often insufficient for identifying objects with complex or irregular shapes. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that enables MVS using multiple views of the target object. Our method employs a deep learning architecture to learn a shared embedding space where each view is represented as a vector. We demonstrate that our model effectively captures the object's appearance across different perspectives. Extensive experiments conducted on the MVS-POD and MVS-POD-IR datasets confirm that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

Real-time epileptic seizure detection is vital for timely intervention, yet it remains challenging due to the seizure's unpredictable nature and the presence of various confounding factors. This paper introduces a novel method for seizure detection using a deep learning framework that integrates a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The CNN extracts spatial features from EEG data, while the LSTM processes temporal patterns. We evaluated the proposed CNN-LSTM architecture against two other deep learning models: a standard CNN and a standalone LSTM. The results demonstrate that our CNN-LSTM approach outperforms these alternatives, achieving an F1-score of 0.9999 and a sensitivity of 0.9999.

The detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from binary black hole (BBH) mergers has opened a new avenue for constraining cosmological parameters. This study examines the potential of utilizing BBH signals to place constraints on the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and dark energy parameters within the $\Lambda$CDM framework, specifically investigating the impact of varying assumptions regarding the population of BBHs. We analyze the $1+1$-dimensional toy model introduced by \cite{2019ApJ...863..113W} to determine how the BBH population influences the accuracy of these constraints. Our results indicate that the BBN population can be effectively modeled as a Gaussian distribution, with the mean and variance of this distribution serving as free parameters. We further investigate the effects of BBN population uncertainties on the derived constraints for $H_0$ and dark energy parameters, specifically the equation of state parameter $w$ and its derivative $dw/dz$. We find that the BBN population can significantly impact the constraints on these cosmological parameters. Finally, we discuss the potential benefits of incorporating BBN population information from future surveys to improve cosmological parameter constraints.

Web-based systems must prioritize accessibility, ensuring that users with diverse abilities can effectively utilize them. Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems, which enable individuals to retrieve answers from knowledge graphs using natural language, are no exception. This study introduces a novel methodology for assessing the accessibility of these KGQA systems, grounded in the principles of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG). We have developed an automated tool that evaluates both the question generation and answer interpretation modules against WCAG criteria. Our approach was tested on two prominent open-source frameworks, Babelfish and QALIBR. Our findings reveal that both systems adhere to the highest level of WCAG conformance, indicating a high degree of accessibility.

To address this, we introduce a framework that integrates a task-agnostic memory with a dynamic task-aware memory, enabling the system to adaptively allocate memory resources based on evolving requirements. We further incorporate a memory management mechanism that leverages a memory bank to store representative knowledge from past tasks, ensuring robust performance in dynamic settings. To facilitate this, we propose a novel learning strategy that utilizes a memory bank to enhance the system's ability to handle diverse few-shot scenarios. Medical image analysis is a rapidly evolving field, with machine learning (ML) techniques increasingly deployed in clinical settings. However, the inherent biases within training datasets can lead to significant disparities in model performance across different patient groups. To address this, fairness-aware methods are being developed to ensure equitable outcomes for all patients. This paper provides a comprehensive review of current literature on bias and fairness in medical imaging. We begin by defining the core concepts of bias and fairness within this domain, followed by an examination of bias sources and mitigation strategies. Furthermore, we evaluate existing evaluation metrics and discuss the practical challenges of implementing these approaches in healthcare. Finally, we outline key avenues for future research.

Although noisy labels are prevalent in real-world scenarios, current Metric Learning approaches typically assume clean data. This study introduces a novel approach designed to enhance the robustness of Metric Learning against noisy labels by integrating the principles of Label Noise Robustness (NLR) into a unified framework. We propose a new loss function that simultaneously optimizes hard negative mining, discriminative feature extraction, and noise identification. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in both classification and metric learning tasks involving corrupted data.

We introduce a novel statistical framework for analyzing cosmic structure that extends beyond traditional two-point correlations. This approach utilizes the generalized $n$-th order moments of the density field, specifically the generalized mean, which serves as a higher-order generalization of the standard average density. By examining the redshift-space density field, we demonstrate that this statistic is sensitive to non-Gaussian clustering patterns at higher orders. We further derive a perturbative expansion for the redshift-space generalized mean, showing that it is sensitive to the same non-linear gravitational effects captured by higher-order correlation functions. Finally, we illustrate the application of this formalism using the redshift-space density field of the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 Galaxy Sample, analyzing the galaxy distribution across the redshift range $0.2 < z < 0.6$.

We investigate the quantum phase diagram of a two-dimensional SO(5) superfluid, which emerges in the $J_{xy}$-limit of the SO(6) spin model. This system is characterized by a unique quantum phase transition occurring between a gapped, symmetry-broken phase and a gapless SO(5) topological superfluid. The latter exhibits correlations that are anisotropic yet exhibit a power-law decay. We demonstrate that the topological nature of the superfluid is confirmed by the presence of a non-trivial topological invariant, which is further corroborated by the fractionalization of the spin-1/2 excitations.

This study presents the design, construction, and testing of a compact, low-cost, and cost-effective scintillation detector utilizing micropixel avalanche photodiodes (APDs) and a photolithographic process. The detector employs a 128×128 pixel array of micropixel APDs (Pixeldetector) fabricated on a silicon substrate, paired with a 128×128 pixel array of scintillating crystals. Each micropixel measures 200×200 μm² and is separated by a 20 μm gap. The crystal array consists of 128×128 elements, with each crystal measuring 200×200 μm³ and separated by a 20 μm gap.
